title: Plan for adding JSON output to the word count tool
summary: Three tasks: add the JSON output path behind the flag, cover the error path with a test, and document the new flag. The output formatting task comes first because the other two depend on it.
rollback_note: Revert the job branch. No data or configuration is changed outside the repository.

tasks.title: Print counts as JSON when the flag is given
tasks.why_this_matters: Scripts cannot reliably parse the plain-text counts. A JSON option gives them a stable format without changing what existing users see.
tasks.what_needs_to_change: Add a --json flag to the argument parser and a formatter that prints lines, words and characters as one JSON object. Leave the plain-text path untouched.
acceptance_criteria: With --json the tool prints one JSON object with the keys lines, words and characters.
Without --json the output is byte-for-byte the same as before.
verification: Unit tests compare the JSON output for a sample file and for an empty file.
A regression test compares the plain-text output with a stored sample.

risks.description: The argument parser may reorder flags in a way that changes existing behavior.
risks.mitigation: The regression test runs the old invocation forms against the stored sample.

tasks.title: Show a clear error when the input file cannot be read
tasks.why_this_matters: The specification requires a clear error and a non-zero exit code for unreadable files, with or without the flag. Nothing tests that yet.
tasks.what_needs_to_change: Add tests for a missing file and an unreadable file, with and without the --json flag. Adjust the error handling only if a test fails.
acceptance_criteria: Both error cases write a message to standard error, leave standard output empty and exit with a non-zero status.
verification: The new tests fail on the previous release and pass on the job branch.

tasks.title: Document the JSON option and its key order
tasks.why_this_matters: Users find new options in the README and in the command help. The key order was an explicit decision in the specification and has to be written down.
tasks.what_needs_to_change: Update the usage section of the README and the command help text. Add one runnable example with its expected output.
acceptance_criteria: The README shows the flag, the three keys in order, and an example that matches real output.
verification: The documentation gate runs the example and compares its output with the text in the README.
